title: English listening set, version 1
note: Original scripts written for Soundstage. No real person's words, voice or likeness. The scene marked needs_native_review uses non-English words and must be checked by native speakers before any language status is recorded.

scenes.title: Neutral narration
scenes.reference_direction: Calm, even, a little warm. Steady pace, no drama.
checklist: Is the pace steady and natural?
Does it sound read aloud, or like someone telling you?
Are pauses placed where a person would breathe?

scenes.title: A calm conversation
scenes.reference_direction: Two tired friends, quiet and kind. Low energy, close together.
checklist: Do the two voices sound like two different people?
Does it sound like a conversation and not two readings?
Is the kindness audible?

scenes.title: An argument
scenes.reference_direction: Rising anger from Ama, defensive and sarcastic from Kola. It escalates, then cools into bitterness.
checklist: Does the anger build, or is it flat?
Is Kola's sarcasm audible?
Do the raised words sound angry rather than just loud?

scenes.title: Grief
scenes.reference_direction: Quiet, heavy, slow. Held-back tears more than crying. The long pause should feel like a held breath.
checklist: Does it sound sad without being theatrical?
Is the sigh a sound and not the word 'sigh'?
Does the long pause feel natural?

scenes.title: Joy
scenes.reference_direction: Bright, fast, breathless. Ama starts stunned and ends laughing.
checklist: Does it sound happy rather than just fast?
Is the laugh a real laugh and not the word 'laugh'?
Does Ama's voice stay the same person through the laugh?

scenes.title: Whispering
scenes.reference_direction: Tense whispers, close to the microphone, afraid of being heard.
checklist: Is it really a whisper, not just quiet speech?
Can every word still be understood?
Does the tension come through?

scenes.title: Shouting a warning
scenes.reference_direction: Panic. Loud, urgent, no time to breathe.
checklist: Does it sound urgent, or just loud?
Is there distortion or harshness?
Can every word still be understood?

scenes.title: A laugh inside a line
scenes.reference_direction: Amused storytelling. The laughs come out of the words, not on top of them.
checklist: Do the laughs sound like part of the sentence?
Is the word 'laugh' ever spoken? (It must not be.)
Is it the same voice before and after each laugh?

scenes.title: A cough and an interruption
scenes.reference_direction: A professional trying to carry on through a tickly throat. Embarrassed, polite.
checklist: Does it sound like a real cough?
Is the word 'cough' ever spoken? (It must not be.)
Does the sentence recover naturally after each cough?

scenes.title: A gasp of surprise
scenes.reference_direction: Awe turning into fear. The gasps are sudden and real.
checklist: Does the gasp sound sudden and real?
Is the word 'gasp' ever spoken? (It must not be.)
Does the mood shift from awe to fear?

scenes.title: Names and a very long sentence
scenes.reference_direction: A warm announcer introducing a guest. One long sentence with a hard name; breathe at the commas.
checklist: Is the name pronounced convincingly?
Does the long sentence hold together, with breaths in sensible places?
Does it run out of energy before the end?

scenes.title: Greetings in several languages
scenes.reference_direction: Cheerful and welcoming. The non-English words should sound like the languages they belong to.
checklist: Do the French and German words sound like French and German?
Does the Yoruba greeting sound right? (Needs a native Yoruba speaker.)
Does the voice stay the same person across languages?

scenes.title: A busy scene with three speakers
scenes.reference_direction: Light, busy, good-humoured. Four distinct voices, quick turns.
checklist: Can you tell all four speakers apart?
Is the turn-taking quick and natural?
Does the humour land?
